text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
-- Pacheco Pereira quit as vice-president of the opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD). PSD leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa immediately accepted his resignation.
-- Expo '98 Commissioner Cardoso e Cunha will present to government ministers today his proposals for activities and expenditure related to Expo for 1997.
-- Taxi drivers threaten nationwide strike next Monday in a protest against their tax obligations.
-- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres angry with Interior Minister Alberto Costa over leaks of information to the media over the crisis in policing.
-- A civil servants' groups protests against the government's decision to raise the minimum wage by 3.8 percent and calls for an increase of 4.8 percent.

-- The paper learned that Gross Domestic Product grew by 2.5 percent between July 1995 and June 1996, according to quarterly figures of the the National Statistics Institute (INE) due for release later today.

-- Foreign companies contacted leading Portuguese businessmen including Sonae president Belmiro de Azevedo to ask them to take part in the forthcoming privatisation of energy company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal.
